writeup: TIC 388939913 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 11.082379 days and a primary eclipse depth of 7.90%, detected in TESS photometry with a signal-to-noise ratio of 154.2. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 24.5, though the centroid offset of 4.6 arcseconds raises a question about whether the signal originates precisely at the cataloged position. No secondary eclipse was detected. One notable caveat: alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true orbital period may be double the initial measurement. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially novel target for further investigation.
